pairs.why: B has cleaner, smoother map art with flat lakes and simple shapes, like the clean graphic real map; A adds shaded mountains and crinkly paper texture, which is the too-texture-y direction.
A keeps the real card's rich green body, lime flaps and soft fabric finish; B is more of a riveted, clay-toy object in flat lime.
A's rover is built more like a real object, with treaded tires and believable parts, like the real taxi; B's smooth rubbery wheels and blocky orange body look more like a toy.
A matches the real cooler's saturated glossy red, bright ice and lively beach lighting; B is flatter, more muted and matte.
A keeps the real card's blue bass-drum hoop with gold lugs and similar proportions; B swaps in a heavy gold hoop and looks a bit chunkier and toy-like.
A matches the real card's chunky lavender stone table, close framing and soft painted finish; B is small, distant and thin-legged.
A is a believable coiled rope with a lasso loop, matching the real cards' soft, rounded finish; B is built strangely, with two disconnected-looking rings.
A's big glowing lenses fill the front and throw soft colored beams like the real light; B has small lenses on a plain oversized tube, though A's extra vents and stripe are not on the real card.
